page.title: Ad blocker
page.description: Blocks ads, trackers and malware for every device on your network.

install.title: Ad blocker is not installed
install.body: Install it to block ads, trackers and malware on every device that uses your network. Installing starts nothing; you turn the blocker on afterwards.

off.label: Turned off
off.body: The blocker is off. Turn it on to start a DNS server on this machine at {address}.

portTaken.label: Port in use
portTaken.body: Another DNS server already answers on port 53 at {address}, so the blocker cannot start there. Turn that one off, then retry.

starting.label: Starting
starting.body: The DNS server is starting at {address}. The first blocklists can take a minute to download.

stalled.label: Not starting
stalled.body: The DNS server at {address} has not answered for a minute. It may be failing to start with these settings. Try again, or turn it off.

portHeld.label: Could not start
portHeld.body: The DNS server could not start at {address}. Most often port 53 on this machine is held by a service that only answers the machine itself; it can also be a download that failed. Nothing on your network changed. Try again.

conflict.label: Not answering
conflict.body: Something other than the blocker answers on port 53 at {address}. Retry to start the blocker again.

blocking.label: Blocking
blocking.body: Blocking at {address}. Devices that use this address as their DNS server are protected.

noAddress.label: No address
noAddress.body: This machine has no address on your network that Polaris knows of yet, so there is nothing to point devices at. Check again in a minute.

router.title: Point your network at it
router.intro: Devices use the blocker once your router hands out its address as the DNS server.
router.step1: Open your router's settings page and find the DHCP or LAN settings.
router.step2: Set the primary DNS server to {address}.
router.step3: Leave the secondary DNS server empty. Devices use it whenever they like, and it would let ads through.
router.step4: Save, then reconnect your devices or wait for them to renew their address.

lists.title: Lists to block
lists.intro: Lists are downloaded again on the schedule below. More lists block more, and break more sites.

rules.title: Your rules
rules.intro: One per line: a name, *.name for everything under it, or /regex/. Allowed names win over every list.

upstream.title: Resolver
upstream.intro: Where allowed names are looked up. The encrypted ones keep your lookups private from your provider.

records.title: Local names
records.intro: Names your network answers itself, like nas.home.
records.name: Name

validation.invalidUrl: Enter an http or https address.
validation.refresh: Enter a whole number from 1 to 168.

errors.notInstalled: Ad blocker is not installed. Install it from the Marketplace first.
errors.tooLarge: These rules are too long to apply. Remove some of your own rules and save again.
errors.noAddress: This machine has no address on your network yet. Check again in a minute.
errors.portTaken: Another DNS server already answers on port 53 here. Turn it off, then retry.
errors.notApplied: Your settings are saved, but the DNS server did not start with them. See the status above and try again.
errors.invalid: Some values are not valid. Fix the marked fields and save again.
errors.generic: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
errors.notRunning: The DNS server is not running. Turn blocking on first.
errors.notAnswering: The DNS server did not answer. Wait a moment and try again.

insights.title: Today
insights.empty: No lookups yet today. Once the router hands out this DNS server, they show up here.
insights.pausedFor: Blocking paused, back on in {minutes} min
insights.logOff: The DNS server is running settings from before the query log, so lookups are not recorded yet. Apply them to start recording.
